title: Spec a simple shared keyspace (guild) using FOKS methods
description:
Add a protocol-tier spec for a Guild as a simple keyspace of multiple keys. Methods from FOKS (device → user → team keys; encrypt team secret to members' latest user keys; cascade rotation on revoke). Identity remains XID + identikey-auth. Do not specify FOKS servers, user@host, encrypted git, or FOKS KV.

Three layers stay uncollapsed (identikey-capability-v1): identity (this plus auth-challenge), agency (Biscuit), data (Recrypt). A guild keyspace is identity/key-management, not a recryption group and not a capability token.

Blocked on identikey-core architecture accept. Cross-link: identikey-core guilds epic; lightning-mesh mjolnir-mesh-st1.
acceptance_criteria: docs/standards/ has a guild/keyspace spec with test-vector hooks; it does not introduce a FOKS runtime or mix Recrypt/Biscuit into the keyspace.
notes:
Cross-repo: identikey-core guilds-as-shared-keyspaces epic; lightning-mesh mjolnir-mesh-st1. Architecture node is identikey-core child; this spec is the protocol landing after that architecture is accepted.
Steer 2026-08-31: spec two guild profiles. House/buyer keyspace: configurable epoch, kick can rekey. Access-node guildspace (identikey-core-trr.2): high churn, long epoch, lower assurance, auto-wrap on identikey login, used for local service-mesh broadcast. Source of truth is identikey-log ops. Postgres is a cache.
Steer 2026-09-01: guild is not a located document. Spec it as a distributed object = the keys that comprise it; admin keys keep it alive. Nested guilds: assign node to outer, create inner (access-node profile). Ops ride identikey-log among holders. Verbs: join/change, assign node, nest — not rename.

title: Record Biscuit as the protocol-tier agency capability format
description: Land identikey-capability-v1.md: Biscuit (not UCAN) is the agency token. Identity (auth-challenge) vs agency (Biscuit) vs Recrypt data-access (PRE). Retire 'align with UCAN-style later' on auth-challenge and OIDC grant. Wallet delegated-capability caches Biscuit bytes. Test vectors remain ikp-6yz.2.
acceptance_criteria: Spec exists under docs/standards; README table lists it; auth-challenge §9/§11 and OIDC §7 point at it; wallet envelope row names Biscuit.
close_reason: Spec identikey-capability-v1.md landed. Auth-challenge, OIDC grant, wallet envelope, and standards README now point at Biscuit for agency. Recrypt PRE stays data-access. Vectors still ikp-6yz.2.

title: Adopt ur:envelope as the canonical text form; demote ASCII armor to legacy-read
description:
Decided 2026-08-07. encoding-conventions.md section 7 now specifies UR as the text form for a whole envelope crossing a text boundary, and section 6 (the PEM-style armor block) is legacy read-only.

This costs nothing to adopt and that is the point. bc-ur declares "impl<T> UREncodable for T where T: CBORTaggedEncodable", and Envelope implements CBORTaggedEncodable. Every binary in the stack already links bc-ur transitively via bc-components. So envelope.ur_string() and Envelope::from_ur_string() work TODAY -- no new dependency, no feature flag. The capability has been sitting compiled into every binary, unused, while recrypt maintained a hand-rolled PEM variant with its own header grammar and BEGIN/END matching rule to do the same job worse.

What UR buys that armor does not: readable by the Blockchain Commons envelope CLI and every Gordian tool; QR and airgap transport including multi-part for large payloads; a bytewords checksum; no implementation of ours to maintain.

What it costs: recrypt identity export output changes. Armor stays readable, and --format=armor is retained as a frozen legacy alias.
design: Recrypt has the parallel change (recrypt identity export, recrypt-wire/src/armor.rs demoted). Coordinate so the two stacks do not diverge on the type string. Do NOT invent ur:recrypt-identity or ur:identikey-wallet -- the envelope subject already carries the type, and a non-standard UR type is unreadable to every tool in the ecosystem.
acceptance_criteria: ur_string()/from_ur_string() exposed wherever envelopes cross a text boundary in identikey-wallet and ikey; ikey export emits ur:envelope by default; armor decode paths still accept existing blocks; round-trip test that a UR emitted here is parsed by the BC envelope CLI (or at minimum by bc-ur decode) and back; UR type is the standard "envelope", never a per-app type.

title: Enforce the no-copyleft-dependency rule with cargo-deny in CI
description: identikey-core ADR-002 states this as a standing rule: 'the protocol tier may never take a copyleft dependency. One AGPL/MPL/GPL dep in identikey-auth collapses the permissive strategy. cargo-deny enforces a stricter allowlist there than elsewhere.' The ADR describes this as already in force; it is not implemented -- this repo has no deny.toml and no CI workflow at all. The rule is currently upheld by nothing but attention, and the tier just gained identikey-log with a large new transitive graph (bc-envelope, bc-components, fips204, two getrandom majors).
design: Also gate the wasm32-unknown-unknown build here -- identikey-log's crate-type = [rlib, cdylib] and the one-host-import invariant in src/wasm.rs exist specifically so CI can check the module's import section, and nothing checks it yet.
acceptance_criteria: deny.toml with a licenses allowlist that excludes GPL/AGPL/MPL and permits the disjunctive expression; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs cargo deny check licenses plus build/test/clippy; CI fails on a deliberately introduced copyleft dep; vendored forks under vendor/ are handled explicitly rather than silently skipped.
notes: 2026-08-07: the cargo-deny half is DONE (954737a) -- deny.toml added, gate passes, and its first run found the ADR-002 violation now tracked as ikp-a6x. What remains on this issue is wiring it into CI: the untracked .github/workflows/ci.yml in the working tree does not run cargo deny. Add a licenses job to it (recrypt's .github/workflows/ci.yml has one to copy -- needs no heavy build, both checks run off cargo metadata).

title: Add test vectors to the identity-tier specs and make them self-contained
description:
The specs themselves landed 2026-08-07 (61a3800): docs/standards/ now holds identikey-auth-challenge-v1.md, identikey-auth-platform-backends.md, wallet-envelope-format.md and dcbor-determinism.md. What is still missing is the half that makes a spec usable.

1. NO TEST VECTORS on any of them. Called the highest-leverage single artifact in identikey-core docs/licensing-and-commons.md section 6.2. A spec without vectors gets read; a spec with vectors gets implemented. Today the only way to read an IKEYW v2 file is to run this Rust code.

2. NOT SELF-CONTAINED. wallet-envelope-format.md references recrypt encoding-conventions.md for normative content (how byte sequences cross text boundaries) and identity-self-signature.md for the recrypt identity shape; dcbor-determinism.md references recrypt wire-protocol.md. The links are absolute URLs so they resolve, but the implementer this tier exists for is precisely someone who will not read an AGPL product repo. The normative parts need restating here, or encoding-conventions.md needs to move too.

Note identity-self-signature.md correctly stayed in recrypt: it describes the recrypt identity with pre-public/pre-backend assertions, which is app-specific material riding on a generic container -- the boundary D-4 drew.
design: Spec license is still undecided -- OWFa or CC-BY + patent non-assert per licensing doctrine section 6.1, listed there as pending. Resolve before the specs go public, not after.
acceptance_criteria: Byte-level test vectors as committed fixtures for: IKEYW v2 file framing (Argon2id params, XChaCha20-Poly1305, header layout, v1 rejection), the Gordian Envelope identity container including unknown-assertion round-trip stability, and identikey-auth challenge/response CBOR. identikey-wallet and identikey-auth have tests that verify AGAINST those fixtures, not merely roundtrip. Every normative claim is readable without leaving this repo. A competent implementer can build a non-Rust reader from the docs alone.

comments.author: Duke Jones
comments.text: identikey-capability-v1.md joined the identity-tier specs on 2026-08-26. It needs test vectors too (Biscuit authority + one attenuation + verify fail/pass). Same gap as the rest of this folder.

title: Publish identikey-auth and identikey-wallet to crates.io
description: Recrypt consumes identikey-wallet via git branch = main, which is unversioned and unreproducible. Mirrors identikey-core-jsv.4 (identikey-auth) and recrypt-c9q (the recrypt-side dep switch). Publishing is also what makes the license claim real: a crates.io artifact carries the Apache-2.0 OR BSD-2-Clause-Patent expression to anyone who pulls it.
design: Publish identikey-auth first (zero workspace deps), then identikey-wallet. ikey is a binary and need not publish yet. identikey-log is blocked on the vendored bc-shamir/dcbor patches -- a [patch.crates-io] block does not travel with a published crate, so it cannot publish until upstream ships (see ikp vendor issue).
acceptance_criteria: identikey-auth and identikey-wallet published at 0.1.x; both carry license = 'Apache-2.0 OR BSD-2-Clause-Patent' and a description/repository/readme; cargo publish --dry-run clean for each; recrypt-c9q unblocked.

title: Publish the protocol tier: crates.io + specs + test vectors
description: The protocol tier exists as code but is not yet consumable as a protocol. Consumers pin git branches, there are no specs, and there are no test vectors -- so nothing here can be reimplemented by anyone else, which is the entire point of the permissive tier (identikey-core docs/licensing-and-commons.md sections 2 and 6). This epic closes that gap.

title: MPL-2.0 reaches the permissive tier via Blockchain Commons (option-ext); amend ADR-002's absolute phrasing
description:
Found 2026-08-07 by the first cargo-deny run in this workspace. ADR-002 states the protocol tier "may never take a copyleft dependency"; it already has one, and nothing we chose caused it.

  option-ext (MPL-2.0) <- dirs-sys <- dirs <- known-values <- bc-envelope
    <- identikey-log AND identikey-wallet
  option-ext (MPL-2.0) <- dirs-sys <- directories <- identikey-wallet

The second path is ours and is droppable (swap the directories crate for a non-MPL path resolver such as etcetera). The FIRST is not: known-values pulls dirs, every Gordian Envelope consumer pulls known-values, and this workspace is built on Gordian Envelope by design. Bumping does not help -- dirs-sys 0.5 still depends on option-ext. The identical dependency reaches recrypt-wire, a crate recrypt intends to publish permissively.

ASSESSMENT (recorded so it is not redone): MPL-2.0 is file-scope copyleft -- the obligation attaches to the MPL files and modifications of them, not to our source across a link -- and MPL-2.0 section 3.3 is explicitly GPL-compatible, so the GPLv2 firmware reach that BSD-2-Clause-Patent exists to preserve is not lost. That is the specific harm ADR-002 was written to prevent, and it does not occur. The rule worth keeping is "no copyleft dependency WITHOUT a recorded exception", which is what deny.toml now implements.
design: Do NOT relax deny.toml to allow MPL-2.0 globally. The named-exception form is what makes the NEXT copyleft dependency fail the build instead of joining this one quietly.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-002 in identikey-core amended from the absolute prohibition to the exception-based rule, citing this analysis; deny.toml named exception kept in sync; a decision recorded on whether to drop the directories crate from identikey-wallet (closes our own path, leaves the upstream one); optionally an upstream issue asking known-values why a known-value registry needs a directory resolver at all.

title: Secure Enclave ML-DSA-87 signer: an enclave-HELD half for the hybrid identity
description:
Verified 2026-08-07 against Apple's CryptoKit DocC JSON (identikey-core-46v). As of OS 26.0, CryptoKit's SecureEnclave namespace exposes MLDSA65, MLDSA87, MLKEM768, MLKEM1024. SecureEnclave.MLDSA87.PrivateKey has init(accessControl:) and init(accessControl:authenticationContext:) -- key GENERATION inside the enclave -- plus signature(for:) and signature(for:context:).

This matters because it breaks the assumption baked into enclave/macos.rs. Today: SecureEnclaveSigner is P-256 in-enclave (shape 1, non-extractable) and SecureEnclaveEd25519Signer wraps an Ed25519 seed under an SE P-256 key, unwrapping it into app memory on every signature (shape 2, the documented compromise). ML-DSA-87 is not enclave-backed at all. Apple confirms Ed25519 can never be shape 1 -- 'Works only with NIST P-256 elliptic curve keys', and SecureEnclave.P256 is the only curve exposed -- but ML-DSA-87 now can be. So the PQ half of the hybrid, usually assumed the weaker link, is the half that can stay in hardware.
design: Availability: Apple documents these by OS version only, with no chip-generation statement in primary sources. SecureEnclave.isAvailable is the documented runtime check -- probe, do not assume from OS version. Reaching CryptoKit from Rust needs an FFI shim; the existing macos.rs already binds Security.framework via SecKey, but the PQ types are CryptoKit (Swift-only), which is a different and larger bridge. Scope that before committing to the work.
acceptance_criteria: A SecureEnclaveMlDsa87Signer implementing the Signer trait, gated on OS 26+ at runtime; ML-DSA-87 seed never in app memory on supported hardware; falls back to the existing wrapped path when unavailable; which shape is in force is OBSERVABLE to callers, not silently degraded -- custody labelling downstream depends on knowing.
notes: 2026-08-07, per Duke: agreed this is very likely hardware-gated, and probing for it and using it when present is a net win -- but NOT critical path. Lowered P1 -> P2. The probe is the load-bearing half: a runtime capability check that reports which shape is actually in force, so custody labelling (identikey-core-zan.7) can tell the truth on any given device rather than asserting a floor.

title: Reconcile identikey-log's design record: Dreamball-* issue IDs and duplicated vendor/ forks
description: identikey-log lives in the permissive protocol tier but its design rationale is tracked in the Dreamball product repo (~/work/WorldTree/dreamball): Cargo.toml cites Dreamball-y4t.18 for the bc-envelope feature set, Dreamball-y4t.2 for choosing fips204 over pqcrypto-mldsa, and Dreamball-69h for the two-getrandom-majors plumbing. Anyone who forks identikey-protocol gets the code and none of the reasoning -- the PGP lesson applied at tracker level, and the same coupling ADR-002 split the repos to avoid. vendor/DUPLICATION.md separately records that vendor/bc-shamir and vendor/dcbor are byte-for-byte duplicates of Dreamball's copies, deliberately, pending upstream fixes.
design: Do not move Dreamball's issues. Dreamball is a legitimate consumer that drove the work; the fix is that the protocol repo carries its own copy of the reasoning, not that the consumer stops recording it.
acceptance_criteria: The load-bearing rationale behind those three IDs is restated in this repo (crate docs, an ADR, or a docs/pq-and-wasm.md that actually exists -- identikey-log/Cargo.toml already references it); vendor/DUPLICATION.md's joint-deletion criteria are mirrored as an ikp issue so this repo can act on the upstream merges independently; identikey-log appears in the README crate table, where it is currently missing.
notes: 2026-08-07: two acceptance items already landed in the in-flight working tree -- identikey-log now has a README row plus a 'Building for the browser' section, and docs/pq-and-wasm.md exists. What remains is the Dreamball-y4t.18 / y4t.2 / 69h rationale: those IDs are still cited in crates/identikey-log/Cargo.toml as the justification for load-bearing choices, and a fork of this repo cannot read them. Also still open: mirroring vendor/DUPLICATION.md's joint-deletion criteria as an ikp issue.

title: Tolerant wallet container codec: accept multiple envelope type strings
description: recrypt D-4 follow-up 3, deferred at extraction. Today the container codec accepts exactly one type string per WalletParams -- 'recrypt.wallet' or 'identikey.wallet' -- so ikey cannot open a wallet recrypt wrote, even though the file format is identical and unknown assertions already round-trip byte-stably. Cross-app wallet management is the user-facing payoff: one wallet, many apps, no app able to destroy another's key material.
design: Write stays single-typed (you always write your own type string); only read widens. Keep the v1 rejection string behavior intact.
acceptance_criteria: WalletParams gains an accepted-types set distinct from the write type; ikey opens a recrypt.wallet file, lists its identities, and rewrites it without dropping PRE assertions; byte-stability test covers the ikey-edits-recrypt-wallet path in both directions.

value: Guild/keyspace spec is ikp-cvu. Identity/key-management layer, not Recrypt (data) and not Biscuit (agency). FOKS methods, not FOKS runtime. Architecture lives in identikey-core-trr.1.
